arxiv-1912-13308.title: Building Confidence in Scientific Computing Software Via Assurance Cases Journal: Reliability Engineering & Safety Systems
arxiv-1912-13308.creator: Spencer Smith, Mojdeh Sayari Nejad, Alan Wassyng
arxiv-1912-13308.description: Abstract Assurance cases provide an organized and explicit argument for correctness. They can dramatically improve the certification of Scientific Computing Software (SCS). Assurance cases have already been effectively used for safety cases for real time systems. Their advantages for SCS include engaging domain experts, producing only necessary documentation, and providing evidence that can be verified/replicated.

arxiv-2402-14405.title: Genericity of homeomorphisms with full mean Hausdorff dimension
arxiv-2402-14405.creator: Jeovanny M. Acevedo
arxiv-2402-14405.description: Abstract . It is well known that the presence of horseshoes leads to positive entropy. If our goal is to construct a continuous map with infinite entropy, we can consider an infinite sequence of horseshoes, ensuring an unbounded number of legs.

arxiv-2405-11535.title: Proving Functional Program Equivalence via Directed Lemma Synthesis
arxiv-2405-11535.creator: Yican Sun, Ruyi Ji, Jian Fang, Xuanlin Jiang, Mingshuai Chen, Yingfei Xiong (🖂) {}^{\text{(\Letter)}}
arxiv-2405-11535.description: Abstract Proving equivalence between functional programs is a fundamental problem in program verification, which often amounts to reasoning about algebraic data types (ADTs) and compositions of structural recursions . Modern theorem provers provide structural induction for such reasoning, but a structural induction on the original theorem is often insufficient for many equivalence theorems.

arxiv-2405-14006.title: Evaluating Large Language Models with Human Feedback: Establishing a Swedish Benchmark
arxiv-2405-14006.creator: Birger Moëll
arxiv-2405-14006.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Birger Moëll. In the rapidly evolving field of artificial intelligence, large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated significant capabilities across numerous applications. However, the performance of these models in languages with fewer resources, such as Swedish, remains under-explored. This study introduces a comprehensive human benchmark to assess the efficacy of prominent LLMs in understanding and generating Swedish language texts using forced choice ranking.

arxiv-2408-15826.title: Topological inverse Anderson insulator
arxiv-2408-15826.creator: Zheng-Wei Zuo, Jing-Run Lin, Dawei Kang
arxiv-2408-15826.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zheng-Wei Zuo, Jing-Run Lin, Dawei Kang. A different type of topological phase dubbed topological inverse Anderson insulators is proposed, which is characterized by the disorder-induced extended bulk states from the flat-band localization and topological edge states.

arxiv-2505-09863.title: Matching high and low temperature regimes of massive scalar fields
arxiv-2505-09863.creator: Manuel Asorey, Fernando Ezquerro
arxiv-2505-09863.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Manuel Asorey, Fernando Ezquerro. We analyze the matching of high and low temperature expansions of the effective action of massive scalar fields confined between two infinite walls with different boundary conditions. One remarkable low temperature effect is the exponential decay of the vacuum energy with the separation of the walls and the fact that the rate of decay is half for the boundary conditions which involve a connection between the boundary conditions of the two walls.

arxiv-2508-08072.title: Parametrizing the Hubble function instead of dark energy: Many possibilities
arxiv-2508-08072.creator: Sivasish Paul, Raj Kumar Das, Supriya Pan
arxiv-2508-08072.description: Abstract In the present article, we propose a very simple parametrization of the Hubble function without parametrizing the dark components of the Universe. One of the novelties of the parametrization is that it may include a wide variety of the cosmological models, such as dark energy (both noninteracting and interacting fluids), modified gravity, cosmological matter creation and other known scenarios.

arxiv-2509-06875.title: AxelSMOTE: An Agent-Based Oversampling Algorithm for Imbalanced Classification
arxiv-2509-06875.creator: Sukumar Kishanthan, Asela Hevapathige
arxiv-2509-06875.description: Abstract Abstract Class imbalance in machine learning poses a significant challenge, as skewed datasets often hinder performance on minority classes. Traditional oversampling techniques, which are commonly used to alleviate class imbalance, have several drawbacks: they treat features independently, lack similarity-based controls, limit sample diversity, and fail to manage synthetic variety effectively.

arxiv-2511-01929.description: Abstract . Human trajectory data is crucial in urban planning, traffic engineering, and public health. However, directly using real-world trajectory data often faces challenges such as privacy concerns, data acquisition costs, and data quality. A practical solution to these challenges is trajectory generation, a method developed to simulate human mobility behaviors.

arxiv-2511-17351.title: Convergence and stability of Q-learning in Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2511-17351.creator: Massimiliano Manenti, Andrea Iannelli
arxiv-2511-17351.description: Abstract Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning promises, among other benefits, to efficiently capture and utilize the temporal structure of a decision-making problem and to enhance continual learning capabilities, but theoretical guarantees lag behind practice. In this paper, we propose a Feudal Q-learning scheme and investigate under which conditions its coupled updates converge and are stable.

arxiv-2511-18277.title: Point-to-Point: Sparse Motion Guidance for Controllable Video Editing
arxiv-2511-18277.creator: Yeji Song, Jaehyun Lee, Mijin Koo, JunHoo Lee, Nojun Kwak
arxiv-2511-18277.description: Abstract Accurately preserving motion while editing a subject remains a core challenge in video editing tasks. Existing methods often face a trade-off between edit and motion fidelity, as they rely on motion representations that are either overfitted to the layout or only implicitly defined. To overcome this limitation, we revisit point-based motion representation.

Here, we report a synthetically bioengineered probiotic consortium (REcN-F/Ca) developed through directed metabolic adaptations of Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) under iterative hydrogen peroxide selection, subsequently functionalized with fructooligosaccharide-calcium carbonate composites.
